abstract: Aschenbrenner argues AGI by 2027 and superintelligence shortly after are 'strikingly plausible,' with massive concentration of economic and geopolitical power in a handful of frontier labs. The essay series forecasts trillion-dollar compute clusters, national-security primacy of AI capability, and a near-term step-change in productivity that current economic frameworks underestimate.
keyFindings: Timeline: AGI plausibly by 2027, superintelligence by ~2028–2030
Compute build-out reaches trillion-dollar single-cluster scale within the decade
Power concentrates dramatically in firms and states that control frontier capability
Labor displacement framed as a second-order concern below geopolitical and existential considerations
methodology: Forecasting essay extrapolating scaling-law trends and intelligence-explosion arguments; not empirical labor analysis.
qualifiers: Tier 4 — influential independent essay. Author is a former OpenAI superalignment researcher with significant industry stake. Timelines are aggressive and contested by mainstream economists. Treat as one anchor in the takeoff-speed spectrum, not as forecast consensus.
